# Welcome {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Four hours. One working AI assistant — yours.

## What You'll Walk Out With {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="promise" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.2em;"}
An AI assistant **you set up yourself** — plus **2–3 automations** running on your
own academic work.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 1em;"}
Not a search engine. A **member of your team** that drafts, summarizes, and calculates.
:::

## Who This Is For {auto-animate=true}

::: {.callout-note}
## KSU faculty — no coding required
If you can write an email, you can build everything in this workshop. **Nobody writes
code** — you describe the steps in plain language.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
We use **Claude Cowork** today because it's the fastest to set up — but every idea works
in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude too.
:::

## The Day in Five Blocks {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em;"}
| Block | You'll… |
|---|---|
| **How AI Works + RICE** | See *why* it works — and delegate like you brief a TA |
| *Practice + break* | Write a real RICE prompt for your own work |
| **Cowork + Automation** | Set up your agent; build Skills / Schedule / Scripts |
| *Practice* | Run a task and package your first Skill |
| **NotebookLM** | Turn your sources into grounded summaries and decks |
| **Wrap-up** | Tally the hours you won back |
:::
